key_insight: Revisiting local feature matching with a data-driven scaling mindset shows that modern training recipes and larger, better-curated datasets significantly close the gap between classical local methods and recent feed‑forward reconstruction models.
problem_solved: Local feature matching models have lagged because they are trained on only a few mid-sized datasets and outdated pipelines; this work addresses poor generalization, brittle correspondences, and inconsistent evaluation across benchmarks.
method: Scale and curate a larger, diverse training corpus for local correspondences and harmonize labels/annotations across datasets.
Apply modern training recipes: stronger augmentations, robust correspondence losses, and architecture updates (attention/modern matching blocks) to improve matching quality and robustness.
Comprehensive, reproducible evaluation across multiple SfM and pose-estimation benchmarks to quantify gains and failure modes.
impact: For practitioners, LoMa demonstrates that straightforward dataset scaling and contemporary training practices yield substantial, practical improvements in matching robustness and downstream 3D reconstruction, enabling more reliable SfM and localisation pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data curation → training recipe → matching model → SfM output (illustrate flow and where gains occur)

paper_authors: David Nordström, Johan Edstedt, Georg Bökman, Jonathan Astermark, Anders Heyden
